Subject: Dedicated inference: isolation, throughput targets & procurement path

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and clear next steps so we can move from discovery into a benchmark-to-commit phase. I’ve captured the pain, goals, and what we propose Redwood deliver in the immediate run: 

Pain points you emphasized
- Latency spikes during morning batch window (95p hitting ~400ms today) that degrades UX.
- Multitenant burst interference on existing cloud endpoints; team needs stronger isolation guarantees for PHI workloads.
- Cost predictability: procurement needs a clear SOW and a committed capacity number before PO.

Customer goals (as discussed)
- 95th percentile latency <= 150ms for short inference (<=256 tokens) at typical traffic (200 req/s peak).
- Sustained throughput target ~200 requests/sec with headroom for 2x burst.
- VPC-backed private pool, KMS integration for encryption, and SOC2 evidence for onboarding.

Redwood proposal (what we’ll run next)
1) 48-hour performance benchmark on a reserved pool (provisional config: 8x A100 80GB equivalent, single-tenant pool).
2) Test matrix: baseline latency/throughput, 95p/99p tail measurements, cold vs warm KV-cache runs, and simulated burst sessions.
3) Isolation and compliance checks: network egress controls, KMS key wrap validation, and audit log export sample.
4) Canary rollout plan: start with a 4-node canary for internal traffic then expand to full reserved pool once SLA targets met.

Procurement path and timing
- We’ll send a short term-sheet and sizing workbook (attached) to share numbers for a commercial quote.
- Suggested cadence: benchmark week (2 weeks from today), benchmark report within 48h of completion, procurement/PO target by May 20.

Immediate asks for your team
- Approve benchmark window candidate dates (we suggested Apr 27–29 in the call).
- Confirm primary procurement contact (ccing procurement@sonderhealth.com if possible).
- Share a sample traffic file or representative prompt set (anonymized) we can use for throughput testing.

I’ve attached the sizing workbook and a short term-sheet. Ben and Marissa are looped for technical and commercial follow-ups. If this looks right, we’ll lock the benchmark week and share the test plan.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — quick technical note on the benchmark plan and expected numbers so you can calibrate procurement expectations: 

- Benchmark config: 8x A100-80GB equivalent in a single-tenant pool (pinned to a dedicated overlay, NVLink where available).
- Latency expectations: for <=256 token inference we expect median ~60-90ms and 95p in the 100–160ms range depending on model choice and batching. If you need consistent sub-150ms 95p we’ll recommend the following steps during the benchmark:
  * Disable aggressive batching for short queries (continuous batching tuned to 10–20ms max window).
  * Enable KV-cache warm runs and prefix caching for repeated prompt patterns.
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s should be achievable with the proposed pool if quantized 8-bit weights are allowed; raw FP16 will have higher memory utilization but slightly better latency.
- Compliance: we can provide SOC2 Type II report and a short checklist. For KMS you’ll get a flow doc showing envelope encryption and key rotation.

Operational plan: Redwood OPS will run the benchmark in two phases — a staged canary (4 nodes) to validate isolation, then scale to the full 8-node reserved pool. We’ll produce a one-page runbook and the benchmark report with logs/trace links.

Happy to hop on a quick tech touchpoint next week if you want to go deeper on model variants or quantization tradeoffs.

—Ben
